newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian far right stands by Chicago poll slogan.
newsitem.headline: Austrian far right stands by Chicago poll slogan.

text.p: Austria's far-right Freedom Party sent a conciliatory letter to Chicago Mayor Richard Daley on Thursday in an attempt to take the sting out of the party's latest election slogan "Vienna must not become Chicago".

But the letter from Rainer Pawkowicz, head of the Freedom Party's Vienna branch, was not quite the public apology Daley had demanded for the posters, plastered across the Austrian capital ahead of regional elections on October 13.

"When I say Vienna must not become Chicago, I am not highlighting failures in your policies, but glaring mistakes in the security policies of (Vienna's) ruling Social Democrats who have been pretty ineffectual against the recent crime rise," Pawkowicz's letter said.
"Our slogan is not an attack on Chicago, but it is true that Chicago has abundant problems with crime like every American city," he told Reuters.
The Chicago Sun Times had reported Daley was seeking an apology from Pawkowicz.
"It would be the same as if we criticised the population of Vienna saying it was full of Nazis," the paper quoted Daley as saying.
Pawkowicz said there must have been a misunderstanding as he did not believe Daley could be so "petty-minded" as to seriously demand an apology.
"We mean Vienna is in danger of losing the uniqueness of its cultural heritage," Pawkowicz said.

"We can understand that Daley does not want the Chicago of 1996 compared to the Chicago of Al Capone...but it's still a fact that the murder rate in the American city is almost seven times higher than in Vienna," he added.
The local Freedom Party chief said he had invited Daley to Vienna so he could see for himself that the city's glory must be preserved.
U.S. ambassador to Austria Swanee Hunt in a letter early this month objected to "the attempted portrayal of an American city as a negative 'role model' and to the implicit xenophobia of the posters".
The embassy sent a second letter noting the ambassador's "disappointment that the posters had not been removed as promised by the party", a U.S. embassy spokeswoman said.

Vienna's state election takes place on the same day as a crucial nationwide poll for the European Parliament, widely seen as a test for the coalition government of Social Democrats and conservative People's Party.
The nationalist Freedom Party, led by Joerg Haider, has in the past distanced itself from Austria's Nazi past, but some of Haider's comments have made many voters doubt his credibility.
He had to resign as governor of the state of Carinthia in 1991 after praising the labour policies of Austrian-born Nazi dictator Adolf Hitler.
